Meeting header: 2025-12-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Alex (CSM), Priya (Sentinel), Mark (Sentinel), Tara (Sentinel Sec), Luis (Sentinel SRE)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in to triage perf outliers, confirm infra access, and align next benchmarks.

[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya (Sentinel): Priya here, Mark, Tara and Luis also on. Thanks for organizing.
[00:15] Samira: Awesome. Diego, do you want to kick off with what we saw in the last run?
[00:20] Diego (SE): Yeah, quick recap — we ran the mixed workload (chat + batch gen) against the dedicated pool last Friday, sequence lengths averaged 1.2k but we had a subset at 6-8k for the streaming tests. Baseline throughput was fine but the 99th percentile latency spiked to ~450ms on some tails, expected ~180-220ms. We think it's related to memory pressure from batching + KV cache eviction under concurrent long-context sessions.
[02:10] Mark (ML Eng): Uh-huh, that matches what we saw. Some requests show huge token generation stalls around new prefixes, like a cold KV warm-up, it looked like the server re-evaluated cache entries.
[03:05] Diego: Yeah, could be KV cache miss storms — also noticed one pod logged OOM events when batch size was 12 with the quantized-13b variant. Could be a kernel selection issue on that GPU type, or the quant path falling back.
[05:45] Tara (Security): Quick sec question — are the logs for those runs available to our auditors? We need to know what is captured exactly (prompt content redaction, audit log retention, who can see full requests).
[06:12] Alex (CSM): We can share sanitized logs and the audit schema — Samira will attach the SOC2 evidence pack plus a redacted sample.
[06:30] Samira: Yep, I'll put the SOC2 summary and the audit log retention table in the thread.
[07:40] Priya: On access — Luis still can't complete the VPC peering test, pinging back 'connection refused' from your endpoint. We shared route tables.
[08:12] Diego: Ok let's verify the customer-side security groups and the peering NACL entries. Two common gotchas: asymmetric route tables and missing /32 host routes for the peering endpoint. Also double-check DNS resolution for the private endpoint — sometimes the resolver isn't pointed to the VPC DNS.
[12:03] Luis (SRE): We did try with our resolver and it returned external IPs, so that might be it.
[12:40] Samira: I'll share our VPC peering checklist but can you also confirm the AWS account ID for the peering? That fix resolves quickly.
[13:15] Mark: Back to perf — what changes can we try short-term to reduce those 99p spikes?
[13:25] Diego: Immediate knobs: reduce max batch size for long-context requests to avoid OOMs, enable prefix caching for stable prompts, and bump the KV cache size / tweak eviction to LRU-per-session. Longer-term: run with a different quant kernel or different memory placement; we can also adjust compilation flags to favor lower tail latency and accept slightly lower throughput.
[15:00] Priya: Can the platform do per-route policies so low-latency chat routes don't get the big-batch throughput scheduling?
[15:20] Diego: Yes — routing policies can classify by route and apply separate batching profiles; we can pin some routes to a latency-first scheduling class. We'll prototype that in the dedicated pool run.
[18:20] Tara: KMS question again — we're using an external corporate KMS; can Redwood integrate with our key aliases and allow key rotation without re-issuing credentials? We need to see key access flow and proof the key material never leaves our control.
[18:45] Samira: We support your KMS via customer-managed keys. We don't store raw key material; we use the customer KMS for envelope encryption. I'll share the KMS integration doc and an HSM/KMS diagram.
[19:10] Tara: Also need the log of admin console access and an explanation of RBAC roles — who can promote a model, who can access logs.
[20:00] Alex: We'll include a role matrix and an exported admin audit.
[22:05] Mark: Any concerns about model version pinning? For the POC we pinned to rw-serve-13b-q4_0 but some behavior changed after a minor rollout last week.
[22:35] Diego: Right, we recommend pinning exact model build hashes for reproducibility; small runtime patches can affect kernel selection which affects tail latency. We'll propose a pinned build for the dedicated benchmark.
[25:00] Priya: For the dedicated run you mentioned, what infra config will you use? GPU type, mem, pods?
[25:20] Diego: We'll run on A100-80GB equiv, 8 GPUs across a 2-node config, dedicated pool with burst disabled to get steady-state. We'll test batching profiles: B1 (latency-first, batch 1-4), B2 (mixed, 4-8), B3 (throughput, 8-12). Also run the same on a quantized variant and attach kernel selection logs.
[30:00] Luis: Please send the exact SSH jump host or access method for the flamegraph collection; our infra team will need to ingest them.
[30:30] Diego: We'll export perf traces as flamegraph + GPU profiler snapshots; Samira I'll drop the link to the run artifacts after completion.
[33:10] Mark: Any quick wins for our end to reduce incidents? We can shorten prompt context or precompute embeddings for the repeated preface.
[33:40] Diego: Yeah precomputing embeddings and canonicalizing prefixes reduces cache churn. Also suggest mixing smaller hot paths on a separate route.
[36:50] Priya: Is there any feature flag we need to toggle to enable prefix caching? We tried toggling 'cache_enable' but it didn't appear to take effect.
[37:10] Diego: There's a per-route cache policy; if the request signature varies (timestamps in prompt etc.) it won't hit. We'll send a best-practice for canonicalization plus a sample transform to strip volatile fields.
[40:00] Tara: One more security note: our compliance team needs the retention policy for audit logs and the ability to export raw logs for 30 days. Is that doable?
[40:25] Samira: Yes, exportable and configurable retention; standard retention is 90 days but we can set an enterprise policy to 30 or longer. We'll include the export steps.
[42:15] Alex: Quick recap: Diego will run dedicated 8k-context benchmarks, Samira will share peering checklist + SOC2 docs, customer validates KMS and SSO, Luis verifies network routing.
[42:40] Priya: Sounds good. Also can we get a cost estimate for the dedicated run and the monthly committed capacity if we want to reserve?
[43:05] Samira: I'll include a rough cost predict in the email — pricing depends on committed v. burst and quantization yields. We'll send two scenarios (on-demand vs 3mo commit).
[45:55] Mark: Any blockers for scheduling the follow-up test? We prefer 2025-12-10 morning PST.
[46:10] Samira: I'll propose that slot in the calendar after Diego completes the run.
[48:00] Luis: We'll re-run the VPC peer tests after Samira shares the checklist and report back by Friday.
[50:20] Tara: Thanks everyone — please redact any raw prompts before sending logs.
[51:10] Samira: Yep we'll sanitize before sharing. Thanks everyone, end of meeting.
